_auto_routes: Every map you have painted a profile for gets class-appropriate bot routes automatically. The FIRST battle on such a map measures it into a navigation grid (saved to offhangar_user/nav_dump/<map>.grid) and every battle after that loads it instantly. Routes are then laid out for all five classes on both teams - three each, down separate lanes - by sending each class to its own depth on the own-base->enemy-base axis: artillery holds around a tenth of the way over, tank destroyers a third, mediums and heavies past halfway, lights furthest forward. Classes absent from that battle are included deliberately, so a map is not left permanently without light or SPG routes. A map you have NOT painted is never measured and its bots behave exactly as they did before. Set false to turn the generated routes off and use only what you painted.
_ballistic_shells: Shells follow their real gravity-bent trajectory for both the gun marker and the hit test, chord by chord, the way the client's own VehicleGunRotator and ProjectileMover resolve them. Only used when the drop over the shot exceeds 0.25 m, so flat high-velocity guns keep the cheap single ray. Set false to go back to a straight line along the barrel: the barrel is elevated to compensate for the drop, so a straight ray lands high and long by about twice that drop - a few centimetres on a 1000 m/s gun, metres on a KV-2's howitzer.
_battle_keep_gui_sounds: Restore the `gui` sound category after the battle-load call to SoundGroups.enableLobbySounds(False). false (shipped default) = the old behaviour. WHY: stock enableLobbySounds(enable) zeroes BOTH `ambient` and `gui` (dev_ref/stock_082/client/SoundGroups.py:76-81), while enableArenaSounds(enable) restores only `voice`, `vehicles`, `effects`, `ambient` (:83-88). The mod calls enableLobbySounds(False) then enableArenaSounds(True) when the battle loads, so `gui` stayed at 0.0 for the WHOLE battle - and `gui` is where the reload, countdown-timer and base-capture sounds live. That is the reported 'half the sounds are missing (reload, timer, allies capturing the base)'. It also explains the old observation that the timer sound became audible only after a broken battle exit: LEAVE_ARENA calls enableLobbySounds(True) (offline_battle.py, next to 'LEAVE_ARENA stopping inputHandler'), which puts `gui` back while the timer sound is still playing. Stock never calls enableLobbySounds(False) during a battle - only gui/scaleform/hangar.py:139 (with True) and battlereplay.py:343 (replay quiet mode) - so this is a mod regression, not stock behaviour. The restore uses setVolume(..., updatePrefs=False), i.e. it applies the player's own saved `gui` volume and does NOT write preferences.xml. World sounds (engines, gunfire, explosions) were never affected: they are in `vehicles`/`effects`, which enableArenaSounds(True) restores. Restart to apply. Marker in the log: 'BATTLE_SND gui category restored to 1.00 (enableLobbySounds(False) had zeroed it)'. Check: reload ticking, the countdown timer and base capture are audible in battle. Rollback: set false.
_bot_ai_phases: How often a bot re-decides where to steer, as a divider on the frame rate. The obstacle feelers are the most expensive thing a bot does - roughly 25 collision rays each, about 750 per frame at 30 bots, the largest single item in the performance profile. 3 means each bot casts feelers every 3rd frame (~10 decisions per second at 30 FPS) while the other two frames replay the last clear heading from the memory that block already keeps for 15 frames. DRIVING and turning still run every frame for every bot, so nothing stutters - only the deciding is staggered. 1 restores the old every-frame behaviour. Higher is cheaper and makes bots slower to notice an obstacle; above 3 they start clipping corners.
_bot_ai_v2: Diff 100. Tactics layer v2, in NEW files only (bot_capabilities.py / bot_blackboard.py / bot_ai_v2.py): the planner finally learns its OWN machine - yaw-dependent gun elevation limits (the stock calcPitchLimitsFromDesc path), turret arc, traverse speeds, reload/aiming/dispersion, BOTH penetration values of every shell, armor by component, mobility - and fire_allowed survives only when the gun can physically reach the aim point; otherwise the shot is refused, counted by reason (elevation/depression/traverse) and the bot keeps v1 movement order. v1 stays the authority for perception, routes, squads and execution, and the order dict keeps its 16 keys, so nothing downstream changes. Also builds the utility-candidate census and per-tier skill profiles (access+noise+reaction) but does NOT let them choose the mode yet - that is stage 102, so the only new variable in a battle is fire_allowed. INERT until diff 101 wires the switch in _offh_ai_director. false = v1 director, byte-identical. Log: V2_CFG, V2_SKILL, V2_GATE, V2_TACTICS, V2_CAND, V2_KEYS, V2_ERR.
_bot_ai_v2_gate_margin: Diff 100. Global scale on the fire-gate margin, in radians. The gate refuses a shot when the required elevation is outside the yaw-dependent pitch window by more than the margin; the base is 0.035 rad with a known hull pose and 0.12 rad when the pose is unknown (order_for carries no pitch/roll), and each tier scales it again (easy 1.5, medium 1.0, hard 0.75). Bigger = more cautious, more refused shots; 0 = only geometrically impossible shots are refused. Log: V2_GATE ... m=.
_bot_aim_hull_frame: Aim bot turrets and guns in the HULL frame. The world aim (yaw + ballistic elevation) is rotated into the tilted hull (pitch AND roll) before it becomes turret yaw and gun pitch, and the shell leaves along the rendered barrel (hull matrix * turret * gun) instead of barrel_direction(hull_yaw + turret_yaw, gun_pitch). The old code subtracted only the hull pitch, which is exact only for a target dead ahead: on a slope with roll the barrel went high on one side and low on the other, and the shell flew at a different angle from the visible barrel. Shipped false = the old behaviour; set true in offhangar_user/config.json to enable.
_bot_anti_herd: Diff 75. Anti-herd: over-focus penalty works at any distance, is multiplicative (score - max(|score|,40)*(1-mult^k)) and a bot refuses a target that already has desired+hard_n other guns (except visible <= close_m or a one-shot kill; never leaves a bot targetless). spare_player=true keeps the old rule for the player (Diff 82: default false = player is a normal target). Log: ANTI_HERD_CFG, ANTI_HERD refused/kept.
_bot_callouts: Diff 85. Bots call like players (needs bot_chatter): 'Attacking X!' on a new target, 'Support fire on X!' when outgunned, 'Stop/Back, X!' to an ally (the player too) driving at a loaded one-shot enemy, at low HP toward a healthier enemy, or standing spotted under alive enemy arty. Warned bots may ignore it (bot_radio_soft). Log: CALLOUT.
_bot_chat_style: Diff 81. How bots talk (needs bot_chatter=true). text = free chat lines (diff 73). commands = native radio commands with icons: help_call/low_hp -> HELPME, help_go/ack -> POSITIVE, advance -> ATTACK; greetings, frags and deaths are silent. Log: BOT_CMD id= ev= cmd=.
_bot_chatter: Diff 73. Allied bots write in team chat: greeting, frags, deaths, low HP, advisory (hold/advance/cant_pen), short replies to each other and to your typed text; an enemy may write gg in the common channel after killing you. >= 2.5 s between lines, 12 s per bot. Log: CHAT_CFG, BOT_CHAT.
_bot_class_fire_ranges: Diff 68. Long-range fire by class: TD fire_range 450 -> 560 (armoured TD 320 -> 450), heavy 260 -> 340; light/medium unchanged (they close in). Before: target choice reached 340-560 m but the gun was only allowed inside 260/320/340/450 m, so TDs and heavies held targets they could not shoot. Local (offline) AI only. Shipped false = old ranges.
_bot_detail: Render detail of BOT tanks only - your own tank always keeps full detail. This is the render side of the frame, not the Python tick: with 30 bots the non-tick part of a frame measures 23.66 ms in offhangar_user/perf_tick.csv, which caps the frame rate near 42 FPS no matter how fast the simulation gets, because every bot was handed the exact LOD distances a player tank renders at. bot_lod_scale multiplies those distances (1.0 = the old look, lower drops the per-frame chassis work at a shorter range). bot_ground_traces are the dirt trails bots leave behind - the most expensive of the four, and 30 bots write 30 trails every frame. bot_hull_swinging is the suspension sway of the hull, per-frame math per bot. Set bot_lod_scale 1.0 and both flags true to get the previous appearance back.
_bot_difficulty: Bot gunnery tiers - 4 levels. bot_difficulty: easy / medium / hard / mixed (mixed=default='random': each bot privately rolls a tier, 25% easy / 50% medium / 25% hard). easy bots lay a wider aim circle, cycle the gun slower, shoot without weak-spot targeting (sometimes not even properly aimed - see aim_weakspot), and are more likely to freeze up or fumble a retreat instead of repositioning cleanly; hard bots shoot tighter, faster, and aim for weak spots. The tier also drives crew training %, equipment loadout and camo (see bot_loadout_by_difficulty) - a hard bot looks and plays like a veteran's tank, an easy bot looks and plays like something just bought. bot_skill_variety (on) adds chaotic per-bot jitter on top of the tier so two same-tier bots still differ. Each bot's roll is logged once as BOT_SKILL id=... tier=... aim=... reload=... .
_bot_fall_meter: Diff 72. Bots take fall damage when they drive off a cliff in normal play (before: only in the spawn airborne phase). Free-fall meter in offline_battle: >= 0.30 s of free fall then a hard stop -> impact into the existing bot fall consumer (HP 8 m/s free .. ~26 m/s lethal, tracks, engine) + marker HP update with reason world_collision. Log: BOT_FALL_METER_CFG, BOT_FALL_METER, NATIVE_BOT fall. physics_core untouched.
_bot_fight_fix: Diff 88. Bots stop hiding from each other: only TDs/SPGs back off at close range, 'impenetrable' needs pen < 0.6 x armour, single-bot withdraw at force balance -1.1 (was -0.65), low-HP retreat at 10-22 % (was 20-38 %), squad regroup only while travelling, squad fallback leaves live fights alone. false = old behaviour. Log: FIGHT_FIX_CFG, WITHDRAW_WHY.
_bot_hill_hold_s: Diff 82. King-of-hill squad (hill = map centre) holds at most N s after arriving (2N s if it never gets there), then follows its route for 2N s. 0 = old endless hold. Log: HILL_RELEASE.
_bot_loadout_by_difficulty: Master switch for the cosmetic/stat side of bot_difficulty (v4.43): when true (default), the tier a bot rolls (easy/medium/hard) also decides how its TANK looks and plays, not just its aim/reload numbers. easy = just-bought look: no optional equipment, no camouflage, and a green virtual crew (slower turret/reload). medium = one piece of equipment in one slot, ~40% chance of a matching camouflage, a partially-trained crew. hard = equipment in every free slot, ~90% chance of camouflage, a veteran crew (faster turret/reload than the tier's base numbers alone). There are no Tankman objects behind any of this - bots never had crew objects in this mod - it is a single float per bot (crew training level) that multiplies the same crew/module time-penalty path a knocked-out crewman already uses, so it never touches the crew-critical-hit system. Equipment uses the real client optionalDevices API (installOptionalDevice/mayInstallOptionalDevice) so incompatible combinations are skipped, not forced. Camouflage is written onto the bot's VehicleDescr with the real setCamouflage API and a real per-nation-customization camo pool (allow/deny checked against this exact tank), the same way a player's own painted camo is stored - whether it is visible depends on the bot's model-build path picking it up, same as any other camo. Set false to go back to the old behaviour: bot_difficulty still governs aim_mult/reload_mult exactly as before, but no crew level, no equipment, no camouflage is ever assigned to a bot.
_bot_mode_probe: Diff 69, LOG ONLY. Every 10 s MODEPROBE prints the share of bot-frames per combat_mode (engage, flank, withdraw, reload_cover, bait_twitch_*, punish_peek, crossfire, cliff_dive_ram, squad_*, radio_*, ...), and at the next battle a 'MODEPROBE total' line with every mode that ever ran. Tells which bot behaviours are alive and which are dead code. Never changes gameplay.
_bot_names: Name prefix the bots get in the team lists, allies and enemies separately. The number behind it is assigned per bot.
_bot_nickname_style: Auto-spawned team bots (not the manual O/P/L spawn keys, which keep their own Bot/Clone/Ally/Enemy naming). 'era' (default) - old-school 2013-2014 public-match nicknames (transliterated, meme-y, occasionally crude), the kind actual random battles from that era were full of. 'callsign' - the previous clean military callsign pool (Atlas-47 style). Network/LAN bots whose identity is assigned by the match authority ignore this and use whatever name the authority sent.
_bot_pathfinding: Bots follow an A* route over the nav_grid instead of driving straight at their destination and grinding against whatever is in between. Needs nav_grid true. Paths are string-pulled into a handful of long legs (a 56-cell route becomes about 6 waypoints), one search per frame across all bots, and cached until the destination moves or the bot gets stuck. The bot feelers still do local avoidance for what the grid cannot see - other tanks, destructibles. Set false to compare against the old straight-line behaviour; python.log prints a NAVPATH stats line with the stuck percentage either way.
_bot_radio_calm: Diff 81. Bots called SUPPORTMEWITHFIRE on themselves every 20 s and recruited 3 squadmates each time: radio_support_fire was 28% of all bot frames (MODEPROBE 07.10) = herds. true = a bot's own call recruits 1 bot and the outgunned support call cools down 45 s. Player commands are unchanged. Log: RADIO_CALM_CFG on=.
_bot_radio_soft: Diff 83. Radio = request, not order: up to 3 nearby allies (<=250 m) each answer with a chance from teamwork (less if fighting); max 2 for the player, 1 for a bot; lasts 12 s; never pulls a bot out of its fight. Bot low_hp/advance calls also reach allies. false = old obedient radio. Log: RADIO_SOFT, RADIO_BOT.
_bot_reaction_time: Diff 70. Human reaction delay: after first spotting a target (or re-acquiring it after >= 2 s) a bot may not fire until reaction seconds pass (turret still slews). Ranges per tier come from bot_skill_profiles.<tier>.reaction [lo, hi]; every bot also gets a personal bias 0.85-1.2; re-acquire costs 60 %. Log: REACT_CFG once per battle, REACT per new delay. false = old instant trigger.
_bot_real_cover: Diff 93. While reloading, bots look for a real cover cell on the baked navgraph: buildings, rocks or a ridge that hides them from the target and up to two other visible enemies (search 22 m for heavies/TDs, 30 m for others). Falls back to the old 8 m pullback when nothing hides them. false = old behaviour. Log: REAL_COVER_CFG, REAL_COVER found/none.
_bot_real_dispersion: Diff 87. Bots aim with the player's dispersion model: movement / hull turn / turret turn bloom (per-tank chassis and gun factors), after-shot bloom, aiming time. Hard waits for factor <= 1.15 (medium 1.6, easy 2.6; x2.5 under 60 m) up to 4 / 2.5 / 1 s, then fires anyway. Hard aim_mult 1.0 (was 0.85). false = old always-aimed bots. Log: BOT_DISP_CFG, BOT_DISP.
_bot_routes: Bots drive to per-map destinations chosen for their CLASS instead of beelining at the nearest enemy - which is why they all used to converge on the middle of the map. Positions come from Wargaming's own bot navigation graph, extracted from a modern client (the 0.8.2 maps predate bots, but the modern maps grew outward from the same origin, so the coordinates transfer). Every node is re-probed against the real 0.8.2 terrain at battle start and dropped if the map was reworked under it; the pass rate is logged. Only maps with a file in offhangar/routes/ are affected - everywhere else bots behave exactly as before. An enemy within 260 m still wins over the route, so fighting is unchanged.
_bot_skill_profiles: Diff 70+. One table for per-tier bot skill. Now read: reaction [lo, hi] seconds. Later steps add weakspot, bait, reload_cover, mistakes, memory_s here.
_bot_squad_cohesion: Diff 76. Squads: members take the leader's route; while travelling a member > 90 m from its leader regroups beside it; a losing squad (balance <= -0.8) calls the nearest squad within 220 m for 20 s (with bot_chatter: 'Нужна помощь!' / 'Иду на помощь'). Fights are never overridden. Log: SQUAD_COHESION_CFG, SQUAD_HELP, SQUAD_REGROUP.
_bot_squad_mix: Diff 82. true = 3 mixed-class squads per team (round-robin, max 5) instead of filling squads in lineup order (heavies together, mediums together...). Log: SQUAD_MIX_CFG, SQUAD_MIX.
_bot_threat_priority: Diff 92. A visible enemy under 150 m becomes the priority (up to +55, no 'too close' penalty, +22 stickiness on the current target). Enemy SPGs defend themselves: the nearest visible enemy within 150 m is engaged with direct fire; within 60 m flee if not loaded. 'Impenetrable' targets and local outnumbering make bots hold position (retreat only when badly outnumbered or under 50 % HP). false = old behaviour. Log: THREAT_PRIO_CFG, ARTY_DEFENSE, WITHDRAW_WHY ..._hold.
_camera_shake_scale: Native camera shake scale (0 = off, the shipped behaviour). The mod used to have a synthetic shiftCamPos jitter which was removed for looking non-native, and that left damage/death/track/ram with no screen shake at all - all four call sites hit a stub. The engine has its own shake and stock uses it: helpers/effectslist.py:411-413 calls BigWorld.camera().shake(duration, dir) for shock waves, and CursorCamera::shake is documented in the BigWorld sources (src/lib/camera/cursor_camera.cpp:730-748) as 'direction and magnitude, a new shake overwrites the previous one'. So this knob drives the NATIVE shake, not the old jitter: 1.0 is a moderate hit kick, 1.5-2.0 is heavy, 0.5 is subtle. Durations per event: damage 0.30 s, track 0.25 s, ram 0.40 s, death 0.55 s. Logged once per battle as 'CAMSHAKE_CFG scale=...' and counted as cam_shake in diag_probe.
_camera_shake_style: Camera shake style. off = no shake (the shipped behaviour after the old synthetic shiftCamPos jitter was removed for looking non-native). vanilla = stock-like strengths, calibrated from the engine's own shockwave effect (helpers/effectslist.py:389-418 reads scale, default 0.1, and duration, then calls camera.shake). modern = the same profiles x1.75, sharper and heavier, in the spirit of newer clients. All three drive the NATIVE CursorCamera.shake, so it feels like the engine, not like a python jitter. Per-event profile (amplitude at kick=1.0, duration): damage/hit 0.11/0.34s, ricochet 0.12/0.24s, nonpen 0.12/0.26s, splash 0.14/0.40s, track 0.08/0.26s, ram 0.15/0.45s, explosion 0.26/0.80s, death/destruction 0.30/1.00s, ammo_rack 0.40/1.20s. On top of the profile: kick (already carries the damage fraction: 0.4 for a non-pen, 0.6-2.5 scaled by damage/maxHealth), caliber (x0.7-1.8 around 100 mm), camera_shake_scale, and a hard 0.60 cap. Logged once per battle as 'CAMSHAKE_CFG style=.. mult=..'.
_chat_dedup: Diff 73. Every chat/radio line was shown 4 times (4 delivery paths each reach the display). One display gate: same line (kind, channel, text) within 0.6 s is dropped. Log: CHAT_DEDUP dropped=N.

They are NOT part of the battle Flash window, so destroying that window does not remove them - measured live over the REPL on the hangar screen (03.10 00:3x): _WindowsManager__battleWindow is None while g_offline_aih still has __isStarted=False, __isGUIVisible=True, __isArenaStarted=True and __gunMarker objects on arcade/sniper/strategic. _leaveArena already calls _cm.destroy() over __ctrls (:12117-12119) and stock ArcadeControlMode.destroy() destroys __aim and __gunMarker and sets __aih=None (dev_ref/stock_082/client/AvatarInputHandler/control_modes.py:664-674), so this is either a leak of already-destroyed overlays or a destroy that never ran - the log tells which. true = on exit call aih.setGUIVisible(False) (AvatarInputHandler/__init__.py:271-274) and per control showGunMarker(False) / showGunMarker2(False) (control_modes.py:47/:50/:782/:787) / getAim().setVisible(False) (aims.py:141), each guarded, HIDE only - never destroy, the same AvatarInputHandler is reused by the next battle. Markers: 'CROSSHAIR_CFG hide_on_exit=on', 'CROSSHAIR leave_arena pre: isStarted=False isGUIVisible=True isArenaStarted=True ctrls=[...]', 'CROSSHAIR leave_arena done: aih=ok | arcade[alive|destroyed]gm1=off,gm2=off,aim=off | ...'. false = today's behaviour (crosshair stays visible in the hangar).
_crush: Passability of destructible scenery for the driving corridor probe. crush_min_speed is a floor on the speed fed to the retail crush test (can_crush: 0.5*mass*v^2 against the object's authored health). Without a floor a bot crawling at 2-3 m/s through a village cannot break a fence in ONE instant, so the corridor reports a wall and the bot holds in place (hazard_recovery reason=terrain), while the nav grid - sampled by downward ground rays - never saw that fence and routes straight through it. 6.0 m/s (21.6 km/h) asks the question the driver actually faces: would this break if I committed at a normal pace. Fences and poles open up; masonry and houses stay walls because their health is orders of magnitude higher. 0 = the old strict behaviour. fragile_passable_health caps the FRAGILE class, which used to be passable unconditionally - that is why bots drove INTO large fragile objects that explode and offer no passage. Objects whose authored health exceeds the cap become walls; 0 = old behaviour (everything fragile is road). Both are read once per battle and logged as 'CRUSH_CFG ...'; every decision is counted in the CRUSHPROBE line while diag_probe is on. The hull-height probe (which only steps over low scenery) keeps the strict answer either way.
_debug_logging: Enable verbose diagnostic logging in python.log (default: false). Set to true if you are diagnosing issues or submitting a bug report.
_diag_probe: Diagnostics only, no gameplay effect. diag_probe=true logs one aggregated line per category every 3 seconds while a battle runs: FIREPROBE (how many bot-frames passed each of the four gates of _ai_ready_to_fire - reload, order permission, range, gun alignment - plus the smallest observed yaw/pitch error against the tolerance the difficulty tier produced, and how many would have aligned at twice that tolerance), ARTYPROBE (bots, SPG count per team, artillery contacts, artillery orders) and ADVPROBE (player_advisory calls, errors with the last error text, results). It exists to answer 'the bots do nothing' with numbers instead of guesses, changes no game state and costs one attribute test per bot per frame. Turn it off for normal play and for any release build.
_economy: Credits, XP and service costs after a battle. The per-vehicle multipliers (xpFactor, creditsFactor, crewXpFactor), the repair bill and the shell prices are REAL client data. The earning coefficients are not - that calculation ran on the server and WG never published it - so what is modelled is the documented STRUCTURE: damage weighted by the tier difference to the victim, plus kills, plus damage an ally dealt to something you spotted, plus base capture and defence points, plus a survival bonus, and +50 percent for the winning team. The COST side is not reconstructed at all: repairCost per hit point is read from this client's own vehicle files (3.54 at tier 2, 5.34 at tier 5, 8.26 at tier 8, 11.17 at tier 10), and shell and consumable prices come from shells.xml and equipments.xml. The income coefficients are calibrated so that meeting those real costs reproduces the era's economy: mid tiers profit comfortably even in a loss, a mediocre tier-8 loss lands near break-even, and a mediocre tier-10 loss costs about 20k. Ammunition (autoLoad, per shell type, gold rounds billed in gold) and spent consumables (autoEquip) are charged. economy_tuning overrides any of them without recompiling (restart only), lower-case: xp_per_damage, xp_per_assist, xp_per_kill, xp_per_spot, xp_per_capture_point, xp_per_defence_point, xp_survival_bonus, xp_win_factor, credits_per_damage, credits_per_assist, credits_per_kill, credits_per_spot, credits_per_capture_point, credits_tier_slope, credits_tier_pivot, credits_win_factor, free_xp_fraction, tier_ratio_min, tier_ratio_max. Empty = the shipped values.
_experimental_features: EXPERIMENTAL toggles - may be unstable or change between versions: map_variety (0 = unlimited maps, the shipped setting; a long session across many different maps grows the client's memory and eventually wants a restart - set 1-3 to cap that), reuse_map_space (saves the per-battle re-allocation but was observed to keep the PREVIOUS map loaded - see _map_memory), preload_bots (warm bot model+BSP cache during loading screen to cut spawn FPS hitch).
_force_map: Testing aid. Empty = the normal random map. Set to a map name to play that map every battle - '02_malinovka' or just 'malinovka' both work. Useful when you have painted a bot profile for one map and want to see it in game instead of waiting for the roll. Remember to clear it afterwards.
_game_spirit: Diff 79/80. The game spirit (vanilla/modern per node: matchmaker, he_splash, physics, sway, camera_shake) is NOT set here. It lives in offhangar_user/manager.json, written by offhangar_manager.bat in the game folder (a console menu). Keys there: game_spirit, spirit_<node>, sway_tuning, camera_shake_events; manager.json overrides config.json. No manager.json = vanilla (0.8.2). Diff 86: there is no third 'legacy' spirit; an old 'legacy' value reads as vanilla.
_gui_step_trace: Bisect a native client crash by bracketing every GUI and native call this mod makes with a flushed log line. Written after the mid-battle crash of 07.10 15:09 (EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION 0xC0000005 at 0x00C66B43, Read at 0x00000000, no traceback, no dump, second battle): a native crash takes the log buffer with it, which is documented in the wreck_step_trace docstring and is how the hangar-exit crash was found, so the visible tail of python.log is not the last thing the client did. With this flag on each call is preceded by GUI_STEP pre=<name> and followed by GUI_STEP post=<name>, both written and flushed with BigWorld.flushPythonLog(), so after a crash the last pre= without its post= names the call that killed the client. Instrumented: the messenger chat calls (addChannelMessage / addFormattedMessage, including the targeted-at-player variant), the vehicle marker calls (vMarkersManager.onVehicleHealthChanged and showVehicleDamageInfo for ramming, fire, HE, hit and player kills), the minimap calls (notifyVehicleStop, markCell, getCellName), the native camera shake (camera.shake), and the per-battle hull sway setup (setPitchSwinging / setRollSwinging / setShotSwinging for the player and each bot). All of these are EVENTS, never the frame loop, so the cost is a few hundred flushed lines per battle. Log only, no behaviour change, never raises. Shipped false = today behaviour; set true in offhangar_user/config.json while hunting a crash.
_gun_damage_lock: Diff 74. Destroyed gun: gun elevation frozen (player and bots). Damaged gun: elevation speed x0.5. Log: DMG_FX_CFG.
_gun_muzzle_from_descriptor: Compute a bot's shell origin analytically from the type descriptor (hull turretPositions + chassis hullPosition, rotated by turret yaw, applied to the vehicle matrix with turret gunPosition) instead of falling back to position.y+1.5. Reading the HP_gunFire model node fails for every bot (GUNVIS2 mzwhy=node_err in 1193 of 1193 samples), so shells were born inside the shooter's own hull with no barrel offset. This is the same construction the player's shot path already uses (offline_battle.py:17452-17460). Shipped false = the old fallback.
_gun_muzzle_node_sanity: Reject an implausible HP_gunFire reading instead of returning it as the shell origin. WHY: on 04.10 15:13 the client died on the SECOND battle start in the same process - after a clean exit into a fully working hangar (HANGAR_IFACE currentInterface=hangar, HANGAR_DATA onVehiclesUpdate=called, LOBBY_TAIL chain already complete), pressing Battle! logged `LAN selected vehicle resolved: ussr:T62A (1950 HP)` and then `EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION : 0xC0000005 @ 0x00C66B43`, the same address as the earlier hangar crash. _lod_level: lod_level scales how much per-frame work a DISTANT, UNENGAGED bot is allowed to cost. 0 = the shipped behaviour, nothing changes. 1 = balanced: presentation distance 220->180 m, a far bot re-decides its order every 0.50 s instead of 0.35, the contact sweep runs at 20 Hz instead of 25 and slices 3 targets per frame instead of 4. 2 = weak machine (4 cores or a slow one): 140 m, 0.70 s, 14 Hz, 2 targets. Nothing here touches the native batch solve, physics_core, damage or collisions - a far bot's rigid body keeps simulating every frame, it just stops re-rolling orders, exhaust, dust and motion sound as often. Logged once per battle as 'LOD level=N far_m=... far_order=... contacts_dt=... targets_per_frame=...'. Restart to apply; compare PERF contacts/ai_order/bot_effects between levels.
_los_ignore_high_matkinds: Line-of-sight rays call BigWorld.wg_collideSegment(space, a, b, 128), and 128 is NOT 'static geometry only': stock passes a filter callback with this exact signature (avatarinputhandler/control_modes.py:491 uses collFlags & 8 to isolate terrain) and queries dynamic bodies separately with collideDynamic. Without a filter the LOS ray also stops on materials above DESTRUCTIBLE_MATKIND.MAX=100 - measured 01.10 as matKind=109 with an EMPTY destructible filename, vetoing 94% of firing lanes (FIREPROBE ready=1408 clear=0: bots were aimed, permitted and in range but never allowed to shoot, and only ever fired inside the 60 m proximity bypass, which skips LOS). true = pass a filter that keeps terrain and destructibles (matKind <= 100) and ignores anything above; hulls are already handled by _offh_ai_vehicle_blocks_segment, which knows teams and excludes the shooter and the target. false = the old unfiltered ray. Before trusting it, read the LOSPROBE line: it names the vetoing material (material=...) and reports ground_dy, how far above the ground the veto point was. ground_dy near 0 would mean the ray grazes terrain and the probe HEIGHTS need raising instead - a different fix. Logged once per battle as 'LOS_CFG ignore_high_matkinds=...'.
_los_ray_budget: LOS ray budget per sight check. 'full' (shipped default) = today's geometry: four height pairs ((1.8,1.8),(1.8,1.0),(1.0,1.8),(1.0,1.0)) and up to six march steps, i.e. up to 24 BigWorld.wg_collideSegment engine calls per _offh_ai_has_los, plus a 0.20 s verdict cache per (observer,target). 'light' = two pairs ((1.8,1.8),(1.0,1.0)), four steps (8 calls, 3x fewer) and a 0.35 s cache. WHY: on 44_north_america with 30 bots (04.10 00:55 and 01:1x, 77-78 PERF windows) the mod tick costs callback med 19.0-20.5 ms = 60-61% of a 30-34 ms frame, bot_loop 11.0-11.6 ms is its parent, the physics floor (~8.1 ms: native_simulation 3.92-3.95 + physics 3.12-3.15 + physics_state 0.99-1.00) is off limits without touching physics_core, and the diag_probe=false A/B proved the matKind census is NOT hot (fps med 32.75 -> 29.70, no gain, inside run-to-run noise). What is left and addressable is the LOS group: visibility 1.36 + contact_targets 1.46 + part of ai_order 1.58 ~= 4.4 ms. COST of 'light': the two cross pairs (1.8,1.0) and (1.0,1.8) are dropped, so a tall observer vs a low hull loses one of four chances - spotting gets slightly stricter on slopes; and the longer cache makes verdicts up to 0.15 s staler. Marker: 'LOS_BUDGET light|full (pairs=N steps=N cache_ttl=X.XXs)' once per battle.
_los_scene_filter: Which static materials may veto an AI line-of-sight ray. 'matkind100' (shipped default, today's behaviour) keeps the numeric threshold int(matKind) <= 100 (offline_battle.py:_OFFH_LOS_MAX_SCENE_MATKIND) and is only consulted when los_ignore_high_matkinds=true. 'keep_all' keeps EVERY contact the engine offers and leaves the transparency decision where it already lives - in _offh_ai_has_los, which resolves the material and treats only real foliage as transparent (matKind 72 LEAVES, or a filename containing tree/bush/flora/leaves/foliage/speedtree/shrub/branch). WHY: the threshold was measured throwing away the map itself - session 03.10 13:42 census over 307 windows: dropped = stone(111) x9,973,586 cf=0, firm_road(109) x31,111 cf=8, grass(101) x1,614 cf=8, ground(105) x12 cf=8; kept = matKind 0 x99,553, undamaged_1(73) x78,921, undamaged_2(74) x7. Ten million stone contacts (buildings, rocks) never reached the veto logic. Live effect in that battle: director.contacts = 27 and 27 of 27 visible=True, a heavy tank spotted at 129.6 m while PROXIMITY_SPOT_DISTANCE = 50.0 (spotting.py:11) - every spot came through the LOS branch. _los_sight_trim: Trim the AI line-of-sight ray off both hulls before testing it. false (shipped default) = today's geometry: the ray starts and ends min(1.0, dist*0.15) m from the hull centres, 1.0-1.8 m above them (offline_battle.py:6719-6723). true = the contract of bot_ai.trimmed_sight_segment (bot_ai.py:602-628): 4.0 m of clearance at both ends, capped at 35% of the distance. WHY: in the first battle run with los_scene_filter=keep_all (session 03.10 15:51, 11 min) 202 of 207 recorded last_solid_veto samples were 'sand' (matKind 103 = the ground) against 4 undamaged_1 and 1 stone, and 200 of those 202 carry ground_dy = -0.00/0.00 - the ray grazed the terrain right next to a vehicle instead of being genuinely occluded by a crest (real hull-down occlusion shows a substantial ground_dy). trimmed_sight_segment was written for exactly this and grep over every .py of the mod shows it is NEVER CALLED (only its def and a docstring mention at bot_ai.py:3470). Only the clearance changes; the four height pairs stay as they are so the A/B moves ONE variable. Success criterion: the share of sand in last_solid_veto drops sharply while stone/buildings still veto, and the number of known contacts per team grows back from 16 toward 27 without returning to 27/27 visible.
_map_memory: How the battle map is handled between battles. full_space_release (on) gives every battle a FRESH space and releases the previous one at the next battle start: the rolled map is always the map you actually get, at the cost of a free+allocate cycle each battle. reuse_map_space is the opposite and is OFF for a reason - keeping the mapping alive and re-mapping onto the same space id was observed to keep serving the PREVIOUS map, so battles stopped changing maps at all. Do not turn it on to save memory; it trades away map variety. map_variety 0 leaves the map pool unlimited; a small number (1-3) picks a stable subset ONCE per session, so each map's ~150-300 MB of terrain textures loads only once. On a long session across many maps the client grows either way and eventually wants a restart.

_native_math: EXPERIMENTAL, default off. offh_math.dll is an optional pure-C helper the mod loads itself through ctypes (no exe patching, no injection). It never sees a BigWorld object - only flat numeric buffers - so no engine object is touched from a native thread. ctypes releases the GIL for the call, which lets the DLL use several cores for engine-free math. native_math_selftest runs a one-shot measurement at the first battle frame and logs 'NATIVE_MATH selftest ...' (core count, affinity mask, serial vs parallel scaling, GIL probe); it changes no behaviour. native_math additionally routes the spotting candidate pre-filter through the DLL with a parity check against the python result; any mismatch or error disables the native path for the session and the python code keeps running. Both off = the mod behaves exactly as before.
_native_physics: This experimental 0.8.2-only build always uses the retail WGVehicleFilter2/WGVehiclePhysics2 stack for authority-side bot rigid bodies. There is no off switch: any native failure stays visible and immobile instead of silently falling back to python bot movement.
_native_player: native_player gives the LOCAL player tank the same retail rigid body the bots use (falls, pushes, slope slides resolved by WGVehiclePhysics2 instead of the python drive). The trainer F12/F7 bench exercises exactly this path.
_native_player_airborne_sync: Bugfix: when the local player is on native physics, _veh_airborne was forced to False every frame even while the native body was airborne, so the fall/ground code thought the tank was still on the ground and kept pulling it toward the surface. true = sync _veh_airborne from the native state (phase='airborne' or zero track contacts). false = current buggy behaviour.
_native_player_full: Player-only A/B: when the local player's native body is active, skip the mod's Python horizontal collision sweep (_check_horizontal_collision) for the player. The native WGVehiclePhysics2 body already owns wall/column contact, and the extra Python sweep is what can 'magnet' the hull to a surface. false = current behaviour. Logged once per battle as 'NATIVE_PLAYER full=on'.
_native_player_owns_height: Player-only A/B: when the local player's native body is active/airborne, the old Python ground-follow must not rewrite veh_pos.y/_veh_vert_vel/_veh_airborne. This removes the second height owner that fought WGVehiclePhysics2 on bumps and descents ('hull jitter' / 'hull sank into the ground'). Native fall handling already lives in the native-player path. false = current behaviour. Logged once per battle as 'NATIVE_PLAYER owns_height=on'.
_native_player_roller_off: Player-only A/B: force physics_shared.ROLLER_MODE=False for the local player while keeping the current server-style IS_CLIENT=False mass/contact split. This isolates the per-roller track contact model from the full client contract that made the tank sluggish. false = current behaviour (server-style roller setup). true = player's native body is built without roller mode. Logged once per player attach as 'NATIVE_SUSPENSION mode=server roller=off'.
_native_player_visual_attitude: Player-only A/B: keep native physics as the sole owner of height/contact, but drive the VISIBLE hull pitch/roll from the old smoothed terrain-follow instead of the raw native attitude. This restores the pre-native 'ski' feel (load/lean on slopes) without letting Python rewrite veh_pos.y again. Requires native_player_owns_height=true to be meaningful. false = current behaviour (native attitude drives the model). Logged once per battle as 'NATIVE_PLAYER visual_attitude=on'.
_nav_grid: Bot pathfinding groundwork. nav_grid samples the playable area at battle start into a passability grid (~10000 cells, sized so small city maps get finer cells) using the same ground+water probes the route system uses, and writes it to offhangar_user/nav_dump/<map>.grid. Buildings appear for free - a downward ray hits the roof, so the cell reads as a cliff against its neighbours. PHASE 1: this only measures and dumps, no bot behaviour changes yet. Costs a few hundred raycasts a frame during the countdown, while bots are frozen anyway. Set false to skip it entirely.

_perf: perf_debug=true writes one row per second to offhangar_user/perf_tick.csv while a battle runs: fps, frame_ms, tick_ms, tick_max_ms, tick_pct, nontick_ms, bots, gui, map. nontick_ms is the interesting column - it is the renderer plus Scaleform plus the rest of the client, everything the mod's Python does NOT control, and it is what decides whether a given frame rate is reachable at all. It also logs BigWorld.graphicsSettings() and the screen size to python.log once per session, because the in-game settings dialog is broken in this client (python.log: 'settingsDialog is not found in flash by name popupNN') and the preferences.xml under AppData belongs to a modern WoT, not to this one. perf_gui_ab is a measuring tool, not a play setting: set it to a whole number of seconds (3 to 5 is a good range, below 1 is ignored) and the battle interface is switched on and off via the Visibility/GUI watcher in blocks of that many CSV rows. The switch only ever happens on a row boundary, so a row holds frames from one state and never a blend of both - sort the CSV by the gui column and the difference between the two frame_ms averages is what Scaleform costs per frame. The interface visibly appears and disappears while this runs, so turn it back to 0 for normal play.
_physics: physics_debug=true logs a ~5 Hz telemetry row to offhangar_user/physics_telemetry.csv while driving (speed, accel, slope, grip vs gravity, turn, slide) - graph it to tune vs original WoT. physics_tuning overrides the physics constants WITHOUT recompiling (restart only). Keys: gravity_factor, cohesion, drive_traction (climb grip, ~0.75 = ~35 deg limit; raise to climb steeper), power_factor, bkwd_power_fraction, traverse_accel_time, traverse_speed_cost, coast_brake_share, steer_resist_mult, slide_max, overspeed_max_factor (downhill overspeed cap, x spec top speed), overspeed_damp (how fast overspeed bleeds back), slope_coh_decay, slope_coh_decay_y, coh_decay_bound, fall_safe_speed, fall_dmg_per_ms, ram_safe_speed, ram_energy_const (Cram of E = 0.5*Cram*mu*v_eff^2, reconstruction - the 0.8.2 damage calculator was cell-side and never published), ram_armor_absorb (HP absorbed per mm of nominal armour at the contact, x spall liner; the shipped 1.25 zeroed every ram below ~10 m/s closing - 0 damage in 51/51 events, session 02.10 15:01 - so start around 0.25-0.5). Empty = WG defaults.
_physics_hz: physics_hz decimates the NATIVE physics batch. Instead of solving every rigid body on every rendered frame, the batch is solved at this many Hz and the accumulated frame time is passed as dt (physics_core clamps it to DYNAMICS_MAX_DT=0.10 anyway, so motion stays correct - only the update rate changes). 0 = off, the old every-frame behaviour. At 30 bots the batch costs ~3.8 ms/frame, so 20 roughly halves it, 15 and 10 cut more; this is the single biggest frame item the mod controls. The batch cannot be split (per-vehicle calls reset it and lose native pair contacts), which means YOUR tank is solved at the same rate - below ~15 Hz the own vehicle starts to feel less direct, and that is the trade to watch. Bot motion stays smooth because their models are bound to the native filters, which interpolate between solves the same way retail smooths 10 Hz server updates. Restart to apply; logged once per battle as 'PHYSICS_HZ hz=... decimation=on/off'.
_player_advisory_fix: Diff 73. Advisory (hold/advance/cant_pen toasts) never fired: it read PlayerAccount.health = 0 -> 'player dead' -> None (log advisory_calls=125 results=0). Now reads the player's tank HP.
_player_bot_style_suspension: Player-only presentation A/B: when the local player's native body is active, drive the visible hull pitch/roll with the same terrain-target blend the bots use (faster pitch than roll, capped roll) instead of the raw native attitude. Physics/height stay native. false = current behaviour. Logged once per battle as 'PLAYER_BOT_SUSPENSION on'.
_player_swing_scale: Hull sway of YOUR tank with the live native suspension: 1.0 = full descriptor strength (rocks hard on turns), 0.5 = halved (default), 0 = no sway at all. Shot/hit kicks are NOT scaled.
_ram_direction_fix: Ram damage picks the target's armour plate by the impact direction, and the sign was inverted. physics.ram_facing_dot returns dot(rammer->target, target_forward), so a HEAD-ON hit is -1 and a REAR hit is +1; physics.ram_nominal_armor instead maps >+0.3 to primaryArmor[0] and <-0.3 to primaryArmor[2], i.e. it expects the opposite sign. Passing the raw value meant a head-on ram was absorbed with the target's REAR plate value and a rear ram with its FRONT plate, while ram_damage's own directional multipliers (written for -1 = front) were correct - so the two halves of the model disagreed and the direction term looked arbitrary. true = negate the dot for the ARMOUR lookup only (multipliers untouched), so front/side/rear plates are chosen correctly. false = the old behaviour. Every ram logs 'RAM ... fd=%+.2f plate_o=front|side|rear armor_o=..' and once per battle 'RAMPROBE veh=.. hull_primaryArmor=(f,s,r) chosen_plate=..' so the (front, side, rear) order itself can be checked against published TTX rather than believed.
_ram_mass_from_body: Ram damage uses the RAMMER'S REAL MASS. _tank_resolve zeroes inv_self for native bodies so the python contact response does not fight the engine's own collision solve - correct for the push, but that zero was then reused as the mass passed to physics.ram_damage, making the attacker 1e9 kg (1e6 tonnes). With an infinitely heavy rammer the reduced mass mu collapses onto the victim's mass (the energy pool is roughly doubled), share_self = E*m_other/(m_self+m_other) goes to ~0 and share_other ~= E. Measured over 233 ram events in four sessions (01-02.10.2026): the rammer took damage in 5 of them - all five the player, whose body is not flagged native_owner - and in 0 of 179 bot-vs-bot rams, while one hit on a victim reached 1644 HP. Post-ram track damage inherited the same inflation because it adds 0.35 of the (wrong) hull damage to both tracks. true = both hulls take damage in proportion to the OTHER vehicle's mass, as physics.ram_damage documents, and the track term follows the corrected number; false = the old behaviour. Logged once per battle as 'RAM_CFG mass_from_body=on|off' and on every ram as 'RAM id=.. <-> id=.. closing=.. dmg other=.. self=.. mass_self=..t mass_other=..t mode=real|legacy'. The kinetic constant Cram=0.58, RAM_SAFE_SPEED=1.5 m/s and the 1.25*armour*spall absorption in physics.ram_damage are a reconstruction, not stock data (the 0.8.2 server formula was never published) - tune via physics_tuning ram_safe_speed, not by editing this flag.
_readme: offhangar options. The live copy is <game folder>/offhangar_user/config.json - created from these defaults on first launch, and it survives mod updates. Options missing from the live copy fall back to the values in config_defaults.json shipped with the mod.
_refuse_post_battle_authority: Refuse a bot-authority promotion that arrives after the battle is decided. The worker exits first at battle end, so the server used to elect the surviving replica, which then started simulating 29 bots with no native bodies during arena teardown and crashed with 0xC0000005 @ 0x00C66B43. Mid-battle promotions are still accepted. Shipped false.
_remote_bot_sounds: REPLICA ONLY (the visible client when the authority/worker split is running, i.e. Start_Offline_With_Worker.bat); in single-process mode it changes nothing because there every bot is simulated locally and the stock audio call site already runs. WHY IT IS NEEDED: with the split, the bots in the visible client are marked _network_remote, and offline_battle's per-frame vehicle loop skips those outright - it updates spotting and then continues (offline_battle.py, the `if getattr(m_veh, '_network_remote', False): ... update_remote_spotting ... continue` branch) - so the normal audio call site (`_offh_perf_call('bot_audio', _sync_bot_motion_sounds, ...)`, itself gated on `not _is_worker_tick`) is never reached for them. The authority does reach it, but the authority is the muted headless worker. Result before this flag: enemy tanks drive around in complete silence. true = the replica drives `_sync_bot_motion_sounds` from `advance_network_smoothing` (network_battle.py), the one place that already touches every remote mock every frame to interpolate its pose and animate its tracks. Inputs are the same as the stock call site: typeDescriptor, the own-vehicle position as the listener (Avatar.getOwnVehiclePosition, dev_ref/stock_082/client/avatar.py:1336), forward speed with exactly the formula the track animation uses, and a signed throttle estimate that only feeds `power_fraction = speed/speed_limit + abs(throttle) * 0.3`. NOTHING is duplicated here: the 130 m range gate, `_spot_visible` under sounds_require_spot, the prebattle mute (arena period != 3), the 10 Hz control rate and the isAlive check before creating a sound all stay inside `_sync_bot_motion_sounds`; dead bots are silenced by the existing stop paths (offline_battle.py:8985 and :10673 'Dead engines are silent'). The worker process never calls it (guarded on OFFHANGAR_WORKER_MODE). Restart to apply. Cost: one dict lookup plus a 10 Hz accumulator tick per remote bot inside the existing network_smoothing stage (measured 1.08 ms in the replica). Check in battle: enemy engines/tracks are audible inside ~115-130 m when spotted, silent when unspotted (sounds_require_spot=true), and stop the moment a bot dies. Measured 04.10 from the outside (PowerShell, two samples 8 s apart): both WorldOfTanks.exe processes ~108-110% of ONE core, 811/874 MB, 53/58 threads, on a 12-core/31.7 GB machine; the worker's own simulation tick is only 'SERVER PERF cpu_core=11.8-14.4% tick=30.0Hz avg=3.63-4.33ms p95=6.85-8.16ms overruns=0', i.e. ~85-90% of that core is render/GUI overhead. true does two things, coupled on purpose so the trim can never be turned on without its protection. (2) Then quality drops to the stock LOW preset using the same engine calls stock uses: BigWorld.setGraphicsSetting(label, value) per setting (dev_ref/stock_082/client/gui/graphicspresets.py:132), then BigWorld.commitPendingGraphicsSettings() (dev_ref/stock_082/client/gui/scaleform/settingsinterface.py:580,583). NOT touched by this flag: resolution, video mode, monitor index, maxFrameRate. Restart to apply (the flag is read once at import). Markers in worker_diag.log: 'WORKER_GFX savePreferences stubbed: shared preferences.xml is read-only for the worker' and 'WORKER_GFX preset=LOW applied=N/17 failed=none'. Rollback: set false - the worker renders exactly as before and savePreferences stays stock.
_worker_render_size: WORKER ONLY (the headless second client); the visible client keeps its own window and is not touched. Format 'WxH' or 'auto', empty string = off = shipped behaviour. An explicit WxH is clamped to 160..1920 x 120..1200. 'auto' asks the engine for its own list (BigWorld.listVideoModesAllMonitors, filtered like gui/GraphicsResolutions.py:20-39 and :61-75) and takes the SMALLEST supported size - use this, because an arbitrary size is silently refused: 320x240 was requested six times on 04.10 15:21 and every readback still reported (1024, 768), ending in 'WORKER_RES GAVE UP after 6 attempts'. With 'auto' the log also shows what the engine offers: 'WORKER_RES auto: N distinct modes, max_windowed=..., smallest=[...]' then 'WORKER_RES auto picked WxH'. WHY: the worker's frame is ~38.7 ms but its Python callback is only ~20.5 ms (measured 04.10 14:30, 44_north_america, 31 bots: fps med 25.9, callback med 20.48 ms), so ~18 ms per frame is engine work - render and swap - for an image nobody ever sees. The worker's frame rate is ALSO how often bot states get published: `bot_updates` med 20.4/s against `snapshots` 30.0/s with `max_bot_gap` med 105 ms, which is exactly the reported 'they all drive at 20-30 fps' stutter in the visible client. So this flag trades invisible pixels for publication rate. It is NOT a CPU lever and should not be sold as one: the worker's CPU is almost entirely the callback (20.48 ms x 25.9 fps = ~53% of a core, measured 51.4% from the outside), so expect fps and bot_updates to improve, not the process to get much cheaper. Restart to apply. Marker in worker_diag.log: 'WORKER_RES (1024, 768) -> (320, 240) (want 320x240)'. Check: worker fps and client `bot_updates` should rise, `max_bot_gap` should fall, and the visible client's own window/resolution must be unchanged. Rollback: empty string.
_worker_window_size: WORKER ONLY, and read by the LAUNCHER (res_mods/0.8.2/tools/offline_worker_starter.py), not by the client - so it takes effect when the worker process starts, no client restart logic involved. Format 'WxH', accepted range 160..1920 x 120..1200, anything else falls back to 1024x768. WHY IT EXISTS - measured, not assumed: the visible client and the headless worker read the SAME %APPDATA%/Wargaming.net/WorldOfTanks/preferences.xml. On 04.10 15:24 the player's client saved its own new video settings (windowedWidth 1920, windowedHeight 1009, waitVSync true; the file went from 12331 bytes / mtime 02.10 19:01 to 12332 / 15:24) and the worker, started afterwards, came up rendering about six times more pixels with vsync enabled. A settings change in the visible client therefore made the whole battle stutter twice as much. Runtime resizing is NOT an alternative: `BigWorld.resizeWindow` was attempted with 320x240 and with 640x480 (the smallest mode reported by `BigWorld.listVideoModesAllMonitors()`), six tries each, no exception raised and the readback never changed - stock only ever resizes to a size from the engine's own filtered list (gui/GraphicsResolutions.py:20-39, :61-75, :244-281). The copy is rewritten on EVERY launch so the worker cannot drift, and the player's own file is never read back into or written by the worker. Restart the whole stack (Start_Offline_With_Worker.bat) to apply. Launcher console prints 'Worker profile: <path> (windowed WxH, waitVSync false; copied from <player file>)'. Check after launch: worker `proc=worker` fps should return to ~26 and frame to ~36 ms, client `bot_updates` back to ~20/s, and the worker's own WORKER_RES/`wg_getCurrentResolution` readings should show the small size. _wreck_freeze_mode: What happens to a bot's native rigid body when it dies. guard = the shipped behaviour: guard_fault() freezes the body AND faults it, starting the wreck/detach transaction - this crashed the client natively on 01.10 (0xC0000005 @ 0x00E78498, a NULL-owner smart-pointer assignment right after the 'wreck freeze' log line; an earlier variant, pushable-wreck, crashed the same way at 0x0090A3EA and is still switched off in the code). sleep = freeze through WGVehiclePhysics2.isFrozen instead: the phase stays active, nothing is detached, the body keeps its EXACT pose (no re-seed, so a dying tank cannot jump position - the 1:1 requirement) and stays in the shared batch as an obstacle; physics_core.wake_mock() later makes it dynamic again, so a wreck can be pushed, fall off a bridge and slide down a slope. Falls back to guard if the isFrozen readback fails. defer = the same guard freeze but wreck_defer_seconds later, so DEATH_FX and the wreck model swap finish first (tests whether the crash is a race with the swap); _offh_wreck_release_or_retry re-asks every 0.1 s, 20 attempts, so nothing is dropped. idle (RECOMMENDED) = physics_core.mark_wreck(), keep the body DYNAMIC with zero drive inputs (no freeze): the corpse still collides, can be shoved by a heavier tank, falls when the ground under it disappears and slides on a slope - this is the mode that satisfies 'a wreck must block'. Measured 01.10: sleep (frozen) dropped collision, the player drove straight through a sleeping wreck while live bodies still collided, so freezing a wreck is only acceptable together with a separate static collider. idle now calls mark_wreck(), the primitive that was already written for exactly this and had NO callers: it zeroes the inputs, keeps WGVehiclePhysics2 live in the shared batch, detaches the entity from its WGVehicleFilter2 and sets the wreck flag that enables wreck_pose(), so the VISIBLE wreck follows the physical body every frame instead of standing still while you push an invisible one. mark_wreck's own docstring names 0x00E78498 - the crash seen on 01.10 - as what that filter detach prevents (the engine dereferences the model when a live filter is attached and the swap nulls it). stop = skip the freeze and hand the body to stop_mock(): documented cost is a wreck that snaps to the bind pose and loses collision - useful only to tell the freeze from the swap. Logged once per battle as 'WRECK_CFG mode=...', counted per interval in WRECKPROBE while diag_probe is on, and every sleep logs its own pose_delta so a position jump would be visible in python.log.
_wreck_marker_rebind: Marker re-bind after the wreck model swap. 'immediate' = fire appearance.onModelChanged() right after the swap (today's behaviour, shipped default): vehicle markers bind to vProxy.model.node('HP_gui') at createMarker time and re-bind only on that event (stock _VehicleMarker), and the swap replaces the model under every existing marker, so without the call the icon stays glued to the deleted live chassis at the death spot while the pushable wreck slides away (enemy wrecks, log 22). 'off' = skip the call. Reason it exists: session 03.10 12:4x died with EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION 0xC0000005 @ 0x00E78498 (Read @ 0x00000000) and the LAST line in python.log was 'WRECK_STEP 7_mock_rebound' (wreck id=1003); between that marker and '8_appearance_notified' the onModelChanged() call is the only statement (offline_battle.py:27226-27231 before this flag), and try/except Exception cannot catch a native access violation. An earlier wreck in the same battle (id=1025) survived its swap, so the crash is intermittent and the 01.10 'wrecks are fixed' result was not absolute. Trade-off of 'off': the stale-marker cosmetic bug returns (markers of the wreck are not re-bound), but the battle is not lost. Markers: 'WRECK_REBIND_CFG mode=off|immediate' once per battle and 'WRECK_STEP 8_appearance_notified mode=<mode>' per swap (needs wreck_step_trace). If 'off' still crashes at 7_mock_rebound, the call is not the culprit and the suspicion moves to the model swap itself.
_wreck_step_trace: Diagnostics for the native crash in the wreck model swap (0xC0000005 @ 0x00E78498, seen in both guard and idle modes right after WRECK_SWAP). true logs WRECK_STEP 1..9 with a flushPythonLog after each, so the last line in python.log names the step that killed the client. Deaths are rare, so the cost is a handful of lines per kill. false (default) = no output at all.
